Writing clean code is a skill that pays off in the long run. The main goal is to make your code readable, not just for the computer, but for other humans—including your future self. One of the easiest ways to achieve this is by following consistent naming conventions. Instead of using vague names like `x` or `data`, choose descriptive ones like `userList` or `calculateTotal`. This makes the purpose of each variable instantly clear.

Another important practice is keeping functions short and focused. A function should do one thing and do it well. If a function tries to handle too many tasks, it becomes confusing and hard to test. By breaking complex logic into smaller, single-purpose functions, you improve the maintainability of your project. When you or a teammate need to fix a bug or add a new feature, clean, well-structured code saves you hours of frustration.
